title: Approve the marketing prelaunch composition
question: These three comps use the marketing screen you selected. Which one should be the build reference? What should carry forward, what feels false, and should it be approved, combined, revised, or rejected?

options.label: Headline with horizontal workflow
options.lineage: The white Showoff prelaunch page with its seven-stage horizontal workflow
options.thesis: One headline and a connected process row explain Showoff before the waitlist action.
options.viewport: A wordmark masthead leads into the left-aligned headline and product description, a seven-stage horizontal icon row, and one blue waitlist button.
options.risk: Seven stages must remain legible across laptop widths and reflow on mobile.

options.label: Copy beside vertical workflow
options.lineage: The selected white, black, and blue system with a vertical process rail
options.thesis: A stacked workflow gives each marketing stage room while the waitlist action stays beside the explanation.
options.viewport: Headline, description, and waitlist action share the left column; seven thin-icon stages form a vertical sequence on the right.
options.risk: The vertical sequence could make the page feel longer and more like application navigation.

options.label: Centered prelaunch hero
options.lineage: The selected minimal Showoff page with a centered hero and process row
options.thesis: A centered headline gives the product explanation one clear focal point.
options.viewport: A centered headline and description lead to the waitlist button; the seven-stage icon row fills the lower viewport.
options.risk: The centered composition can feel more generic than the selected left-aligned screen.
